section_notes: This passage (Zechariah 5:1-11) presents two interconnected visions: the flying scroll (vv. 1-4) and the woman in the ephah (vv. 5-11). The scroll carries a curse against thieves and false swearers; the ephah contains 'Wickedness' personified as a woman, who is carried to Shinar (Babylon) for permanent installation.

The word איפה (ephah) appears repeatedly and was consistently chosen as H374 (a dry measure/container) rather than H375 ('where?') because it always carries the article and functions as a concrete noun in the vision.

The consonants ארא in verse 9 present a difficulty: the only dictionary candidate listed is H690 (a proper name 'Ara'), but the context clearly requires H7200 'to see'. This is a well-known orthographic variation of the 1cs imperfect of ראה.

The verb נקה in verse 3 (Niphal) carries a dual semantic range — both 'acquitted/cleansed' and 'cut off/purged'. The curse context indicates the destructive sense: those who transgress will be purged from the community.

Zechariah 5:3: The verb נקה in Niphal carries an ambiguity: it can mean 'acquitted/held innocent' or 'cut off/extirpated'. The curse context strongly favors the destructive sense — those who steal or swear falsely will be purged out.
Zechariah 5:6: The phrase 'this is their eye in all the land' is striking. The word עין can mean 'eye' or 'appearance/aspect'. The sense seems to be that the ephah represents the visible character or appearance of the people across the land.

Zechariah 5:1: הנה: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. In a vision narrative where something suddenly appears, H2009 'lo!' fits as the exclamation introducing the scroll.
מגלה: H4039 'a roll/scroll' vs H4040 (Aramaic equivalent). H4039 is the Hebrew form and fits this Hebrew text.
Zechariah 5:2: אל/י: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/toward'. With a first-person suffix and following speech, H413 'to me' is the natural directional preposition.
אתה: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you (2ms)'. The morph hint says 2ms pronoun and the context is a question addressed to the prophet; H859 'you' fits.
ראה (first): H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7203 'seer/vision'. Morphology is participle masculine singular; in context of 'What are you seeing?', H7200 as participle 'seeing' fits.
אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'ship/fleet'. The prophet is responding to a question; H589 'I' is the obvious choice.
ראה (second): Same as above; H7200 participle 'seeing'.
ב/אמה (both): H519 'maidservant', H520 'cubit', H521 (Aramaic cubit), H523 'nation'. In context of measuring dimensions (twenty... ten...), H520 'cubit' is the clear choice.
רחב: H7337 'to broaden', H7338 'a width', H7339 'avenue', H7341 'width', H7342 'roomy'. With possessive suffix and parallel to 'length', H7341 'width' is the correct nominal form.
עשר: H6235 'ten', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth'. Following the dimension pattern (twenty cubits length, __ cubits width), H6235 'ten' is clearly correct.
Zechariah 5:3: ה/אלה: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation/curse', H424 'oak', H426 'God (Aramaic)', H428 'these/those'. With the article prefix and as predicate noun ('this is the ___'), H423 'curse' fits the context of a flying scroll bearing judgment over the land.
על: H5920 'the top/Most High', H5921 'over/upon', H5923 'yoke'. Governing 'the face of all the land', H5921 'over' is the spatial preposition needed.
כל (all instances): H3605 'the whole/every' vs H3606 (Aramaic). Hebrew text uses H3605.
ה/גנב: H1589 'to thieve' vs H1590 'a thief'. With the article and participle morphology ('the one stealing'), H1589 as participle form fits.
מ/זה (both): H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. With preposition מ meaning 'from', H2088 'this' makes sense as 'from this [side]'.
כמו/ה (both): H3644 'as/according to' with 3fs suffix, meaning 'according to it' — referring back to the scroll/curse.

נקה (both): H5352 'to be clean/acquit/cut off'. The Niphal (passive) form means 'has been cleaned out' or 'purged/cut off'. The verb carries both senses of acquittal and extirpation; in the context of a curse against thieves and false swearers, the 'cut off/purged' sense applies.
Zechariah 5:4: נאם: H5001 'to whisper/utter as oracle' vs H5002 'an oracle/declaration'. As a construct noun ('declaration of YHWH'), H5002 fits.

ו/באה: The candidate listed is H872 'an entrance', but the traditional ID is H935 'to come/enter'. The verb באה as Qal perfect 3fs of בוא (H935) makes contextual sense — the curse 'has come/entered' the house.
אל (both): H413 'to/toward' — directional preposition governing 'the house of'.
ה/גנב: H1589 'to thieve' vs H1590 'a thief'. Here the morphology is noun ('the thief'), so H1590 fits.
ל/שקר: H8265 'to ogle', H8266 'to be untrue', H8267 'an untruth/falsehood'. With the preposition ל and as adverbial modifier of swearing, H8267 'falsely/falsehood' fits.
בית (all instances): H1004 'house' — the standard Hebrew form.
את (both instances): H853 definite object marker — introducing the objects 'its timbers' and 'its stones'.
Zechariah 5:5: ה/מלאך: H4397 'messenger/angel' vs H4398 (Aramaic). Hebrew form H4397.
ה/דבר: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Participle with article ('the one speaking'), H1696 fits.
נא: H4994 'now/I pray' vs H4995 'raw' vs H4996 'No (Thebes)'. As a particle of entreaty attached to the imperative 'lift', H4994 is correct.
ראה: H7200 'to see' — imperative form here.
ה/זאת: H2063 'this' — feminine demonstrative referring to the thing going out.
Zechariah 5:6: ה/איפה: H374 'ephah (a measure)' vs H375 'what place?/where?'. The article ה- plus the context of identifying a visible object favors H374 'ephah' — a measuring container.

עינ/ם: The consonants עינ with 3mp suffix. H5869 'eye/appearance'. With the possessive 'their', this likely means 'their eye/appearance' — i.e., the visible likeness or aspect of the people throughout the land.
Zechariah 5:7: הנה: H2009 'lo!/behold' — introducing the next element of the vision.
ככר: H3603 'a circle/disc/talent/loaf' vs H3604 (Aramaic). In context of a lead object serving as a lid, H3603 as 'disc/talent' (a round, weighty object) fits.
נשאת: H5379 'something lifted/carried' — passive participle feminine, describing the lead disc being lifted up to reveal what is inside.

אשה: H800 'fire', H801 'burnt offering', H802 'woman'. The subject is described as 'one' (feminine) 'sitting in the midst of the ephah' — H802 'woman' produces a coherent image of a figure seated inside the container.
Zechariah 5:8: ה/רשעה: H7564 'wickedness/wrong' — with the article, 'the wickedness'.
את/ה: H853 object marker with 3fs suffix — 'her'.
אל (first): H413 'into' — direction of the throwing.
אבן: H68 'stone' vs H69 (Aramaic) vs H70 'potter's wheel/stool'. In construct with 'lead', H68 'stone' makes sense as a weighty object — a stone/weight of lead.
אל (second): H413 'onto/toward' — the lead weight is thrown onto the mouth of the ephah.
Zechariah 5:9: ו/ארא: The candidates list only H690 'Ara (a name)', but the traditional ID is H7200 'to see'. The consonants ארא with waw-consecutive match a 1cs form of ראה; this is a common spelling variation. Choosing H7200 'and I saw'.
הנה: H2009 'lo!/behold' — introducing the vision element.
רוח: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room/space', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit'. With the preposition 'in their wings', H7307 'wind' produces the image of wind filling their wings — enabling flight.
ו/ל/הנה: H2007 'them/they' vs H2009 'behold'. With the preposition ל and 3fp suffix, H2007 'to them/they had' fits — describing what belonged to these women.
ה/חסידה: H2624 'stork' — the maternal/kind bird with large wings, providing the simile for the women's wings.
בין... ו/בין: H996 'between' — used twice to form 'between X and Y'.
Zechariah 5:10: אל: H413 'to' — directional preposition toward the messenger.
ה/דבר: H1696 'to speak' — participle 'the one speaking'.

אנה: The candidates show H578 'to groan' and H579 'to approach/meet'. However, the traditional ID is H575 (not listed in candidates) meaning 'where?/whither?'. The consonants אנה support an interrogative adverb 'where/whither'. In context of asking about the destination of the ephah, 'where?' is the only reading that makes sense.

המה: The candidate listed is H1993 'to make a loud sound/rage'. However, the traditional ID is H1992 'they' (3mp pronoun). The consonants המה can be the pronoun 'they'. In context ('where are they carrying'), the pronoun H1992 fits.
Zechariah 5:11: שנער: H8152 'Shinar' — the plain in Babylonia.
שם: H8033 'there' vs H8034 'name' vs H8035 'Shem'. As an adverb of place following the verbs of establishing and setting, H8033 'there' is correct.
מכנת/ה: H4369 'a base/pedestal' with 3fs suffix — 'its base'. This refers to the permanent resting place prepared for the ephah.
